note: Builder data of tools/content/modules/mech_dark*.mjs. Every number is a design target (spec: proposed); every player-visible text is Aoaz's own. Names resolve to tags through countries.json.

text.zin_dark_raids_desc: The war-clans are fed by what the warriors bring home. A raid is not a war, and the Warking knows the difference even when the clans do not: it is a fire lit on a neighbour's roof to warm his own hall. Border tension stands at §Y[?global.zin_dark_border_tension|0]§! of a hundred.
text.zin_dark_horde_desc: Goldoroth is a kingdom of clans, and the Warking rules only as long as they are fed and heard. Four blocs bring their wants to the moot: the Volcano Clans, the Iron Clans, the War-Clans and the Goblin Warrens. Temper stands at §Y[?zin_goldoroth_temper|0]§! of a hundred.
text.zin_dark_sway_desc: The free holds answer to no king, but a hall that has taken black iron, married a chief's daughter and watched the host ride past is a hall that listens. Sway stands high in some, low in others, and Cocanoor counts every hand.
text.zin_dark_accord_desc: Notbuton keeps the Accord alive with beacons, blood-prices and friends across the straits. Its resolve stands at §Y[?global.zin_dark_accord_resolve|0]§! of a hundred.
text.zin_dark_free_holds_desc: The halls of the Dark Lands answer to nobody, and a few of them have learned that being nobody's is easier in company. The Free Moot is a league that stays free; the troll-kin are a people that can be hired. [ROOT.zin_dark_sway_line]
text.zin_dark_straits_desc: Two narrow waters join the Dark Lands to the North Lands and the Middle Lands. Whoever holds a shore may levy a toll, and whoever holds both may close the water altogether.
text.zin_dark_raid_marches_desc: Send the war-clans over the border into Dondor's marches for thirty days. They come back with iron, cattle and stories, and the temper of the clans falls. Dondor is told, and border tension rises. No war is declared.
text.zin_dark_raid_hold_desc: A hold on the border has been slow to see where its interest lies. Thirty days of fire and plunder will help it see. If Goldoroth's host is three times the hold's, the hold bends a little; if not, it hardens.
text.zin_dark_corsair_raid_desc: Black-sailed galleys cross the Sea of Darkness to burn a harbour. Wealth comes home in the holds, and a tension of its own goes out over the water. If the harbour is Blackton's, Lerendor will remember.
text.zin_dark_clash_on_the_march_desc: Not a raid and not a war: the host rides to the border forts and tries them, for as long as the forts hold. The Gathering Dark stirs when banners meet.
text.zin_dark_great_moot_desc: The chiefs of the four blocs gather around the fire at Cocanoor, and each says what the Warking has not given them. One of them will leave better pleased than the rest.
text.zin_dark_feast_the_clans_desc: Oxen on spits, casks of black mead and a share of the armoury's iron given out in handfuls. For a night every bloc remembers it is part of one host. The temper of the clans falls.
text.zin_dark_blood_contest_desc: Champions of the clans fight in the pit until one yields or does not. The watching warriors roar their temper out, and the war-clans think better of their Warking for it.
text.zin_dark_send_gifts_desc: Blades, mail and a keg of the forge's best for the chief of a free hold. They are not payment. They are a reminder of where the good iron comes from.
text.zin_dark_bind_by_marriage_desc: The Warking's kin are offered to the chief of a hold, or the chief's to the Warking. Orc halls hold marriages as seriously as feuds, and the two are very alike. Sway with that hold rises sharply, once.
text.zin_dark_show_the_host_desc: The host is marched in column past a hold's gates, banners up. Nobody is hurt, and everybody remembers. This needs a host at least three times the hold's.
text.zin_dark_offer_iron_yoke_desc: A hold that leans toward Cocanoor is offered the Iron Yoke: to become Goldoroth's tributary, to pay and to host, and to be defended. It may bend the knee or refuse, and a refusal is not forgotten.
text.zin_dark_one_fire_desc: A tributary that has served long and well is taken wholly into the kingdom. Its hearth fire is put out and relit from the Fire-Mountain, and its hall is Goldoroth's.
text.zin_dark_hunt_envoys_desc: Riders from Nafeher have been to the hold with gifts and promises. The Warking's wardens ride out to find them, and the hold remembers who sent the wardens. The south will learn that the hunt was noticed.
text.zin_dark_light_beacons_desc: The beacon chain along the dark coast is lit from end to end. Every hall in the Accord sees it and remembers why it is an Accord. Resolve rises.
text.zin_dark_pay_blood_price_desc: Gold and cattle sent to Cocanoor for the dead of the last raid. It is humiliating and it works: the border cools, and the Warking's clans see silver where they wanted blood.
text.zin_dark_invite_to_accord: Invite a Hold into the Accord
text.zin_dark_invite_to_accord_desc: An orc hold that has seen Cocanoor's fires from its wall is asked to take a seat in the Accord. It may find a seat in a human-led league humbling or sensible.
text.zin_dark_muster_brutes_desc: Dondor's Brutes are called from the hill farms for half a year: big, slow men who hold a line the way a cliff holds a sea.
text.zin_dark_petition_parim_desc: Notbuton sends an envoy to the Golden King. Parim may bless, guarantee or invite, and which it chooses says much about Parim.
text.zin_dark_call_on_the_north_desc: Ships are asked of Sonargur, across the dark water. Lerendor has its own quarrels, and its own reasons to dislike an orc kingdom on the strait.
text.zin_dark_call_free_moot_desc: The holds that answer to no one meet at the moot stone and agree, for the first time in living memory, to answer together when one of them is attacked. It is an oath between neighbours, not a crown.
text.zin_dark_leave_free_moot_desc: The hall withdraws its stone from the moot. It will be remembered, and it will be free of the call.
text.zin_dark_hire_troll_kin_desc: The Forest Nobody Enters sells strength by the season, to those who send iron and honest dealing first. Troy the Old does not take orders and does not give refunds.
text.zin_dark_levy_shore_tolls_desc: A strait whose shore is Goldoroth's pays Goldoroth for the passage. The far shore will not like it, and will not forget.
text.zin_dark_close_strait_desc: In a war, a held shore can bar the water to the enemy's ships altogether. The wardens chain the strait and the galleys stay in harbour.
text.zin_dark_tt_sway_up: Cocanoor's sway over the target rises.
text.zin_dark_tt_hunt: The target's pact with the south falls by one, and the south is told.
text.zin_dark_tt_blood: Border tension falls by 15. Goldoroth is paid in Authority.
text.zin_dark_tt_tolls_paid: The far shore will resent the toll.
text.zin_dark_tt_challenge: The Warking fights the challenger in the pit. The more the War-Clans favour him, the likelier he is to win. If he falls, the chief of the heir's bloc, or else the challenger, is the new Warking.
text.zin_dark_tt_cooldown: The last such order was given too recently.
text.zin_dark_tt_no_clash: No clash is being fought on the march.
text.zin_dark_tt_war_floor: The armed peace has lasted long enough to be tested.
text.zin_dark_tt_outnumber: Goldoroth's host is at least three times the target's.
text.zin_dark_tt_yoke_date: Cocanoor is ready to offer the Iron Yoke.
text.zin_dark_tt_yoke_sway: Cocanoor's sway over the hold is at least 50.
text.zin_dark_tt_yoke_sway_cheap: Cocanoor's sway over the hold is at least 40.
text.zin_dark_tt_one_fire: The hold has borne the Iron Yoke for a year, and Cocanoor's sway over it is at least 80.
text.zin_dark_tt_one_fire_hard: The hold has borne the Iron Yoke for half a year, and Cocanoor's sway over it is at least 70.
text.zin_dark_tt_muster: Border tension is at least 60, or Dondor is at war with Goldoroth.
text.zin_dark_tt_moot_free: This hall is free, owes Cocanoor nothing, and is not bound to the south.
text.zin_dark_tt_moot_none: No Free Moot meets at the stone.
text.zin_dark_tt_moot_cause: Goldoroth holds a third of the Dark Lands, holds a cause of war against a hold, or makes war on one.
text.zin_dark_tt_trolls: The troll-kin think well enough of this hall, or already sell to it.
text.zin_dark_tt_tolls: Goldoroth holds the whole Dark shore of a strait and is at peace with the far shore.
text.zin_dark_tt_close: Goldoroth holds the whole Dark shore of a strait.
text.zin_dark_restless_clans_desc: The war-clans have sat too long by their fires. They sharpen things.
text.zin_dark_settled_hearths_desc: The clans are full and drowsy, and the Warking's calm is worth more than his war.
text.zin_dark_boon_volcano_desc: The Volcano Clans read the smoke above the Fire-Mountain and find it kind to the king.
text.zin_dark_boon_iron_desc: The Iron Clans work the forges day and night in the Warking's favour.
text.zin_dark_boon_war_desc: The warriors are loyal and eager, and have been told they will not be disappointed.
text.zin_dark_boon_warrens_desc: From the Goblin Warrens come numbers that the moot had forgotten it could count.
text.zin_dark_sulk_volcano_desc: The Volcano Clans say the smoke has turned its face from the king.
text.zin_dark_sulk_iron_desc: The Iron Clans bank their fires and keep the best iron for themselves.
text.zin_dark_sulk_war_desc: The warriors have been promised raids and have been handed feasts.
text.zin_dark_sulk_warrens_desc: The Goblin Warrens have gone deeper into the rock and sent no messages.
text.zin_dark_tributary_hold_desc: The hold pays and hosts for Cocanoor, and Cocanoor defends it.
text.zin_dark_free_moot_desc: The hall has sworn to ride when a neighbour of the Moot is attacked.
text.zin_dark_forest_nobody_enters_desc: Armies that have gone into the Troll Forest came out thinner, or did not. The trees are not what hurts them.
text.zin_dark_troll_hirelings_desc: Troll-kin walk with the host for a year. They break whatever stands in their way, and they break their rations too.
text.zin_dark_brutes_mustered_desc: Dondor's hill-farm Brutes stand in the line, as slow to move and as slow to break as a cliff.
text.zin_dark_sea_master: Master of the Sea of Darkness
text.zin_dark_sea_master_desc: Nobody on this coast keeps more harbours, or watches more water.
text.zin_dark_strait_closed_desc: The chain is across the water, and the galleys wait in harbour.
text.zin_dark_watch_the_shore_desc: Beacons are lit on every headland, and the sea forts are manned day and night.
text.zin_dark_accord_shield_desc: The firmer the Accord holds together, the harder its members are to break.
text.zin_dark_troll_woods_desc: A supply train that enters these trees does not come out the same size.
text.zin_trait_black_iron_warlord_desc: Leads from the front in iron the colour of old blood.
text.zin_trait_forge_mistress_desc: Knows every anvil in the Iron Clans by its voice.
text.zin_horde_button_tt: Open or close the Horde of Cocanoor: temper, the four blocs, unity and the border.
text.zin_horde_tab_1_tt: Temper, the four blocs, unity and the border.
text.zin_horde_tab_2_tt: Cocanoor's sway over the halls of the Dark Lands.
text.zin_horde_temper_tt: How hot the blood of the Horde runs. Above 70 it is restless; at 90 it wants blood; below 25 it settles.
text.zin_horde_bloc_volcano_tt: The favour of the Volcano Clans. At 75 the bloc gives its blessing; below 25 it sulks; at 10 its chief may challenge the Warking.
text.zin_horde_bloc_iron_tt: The favour of the Iron Clans. At 75 the bloc gives its blessing; below 25 it sulks; at 10 its chief may challenge the Warking.
text.zin_horde_bloc_war_tt: The favour of the War-Clans. At 75 the bloc gives its blessing; below 25 it sulks; at 10 its chief may challenge the Warking.
text.zin_horde_bloc_warrens_tt: The favour of the Goblin Warrens. At 75 the bloc gives its blessing; below 25 it sulks; at 10 its chief may challenge the Warking.
text.zin_horde_heir_tt: The Warking's heir comes from this bloc.
text.zin_horde_unity: Unity: §Y[?zin_goldoroth_unity|0]§! of 100 of the Dark Lands held
text.zin_horde_unity_tt: The share of the Dark Lands that Cocanoor holds.
text.zin_horde_border_tt: The tension on the border between Cocanoor and the Accord.
text.zin_horde_sway_head_tt: Every hall of the Dark Lands outside Cocanoor and Dondor, with Cocanoor's sway over it and its band.
text.zin_horde_sway_row_tt: A hall of the Dark Lands: Cocanoor's sway over it, from 0 to 100, and its band.
text.zin_accord_button_tt: Open or close the Dark Sea Accord: resolve, the border and the members.
text.zin_accord_resolve_tt: At 60 the Accord holds firm and Goldoroth thinks twice. Below 20 its members begin to leave.
text.zin_accord_border_tt: The tension on the border between the Accord and Cocanoor.
text.zin_accord_member_row_tt: A realm of the Dark Sea Accord.
text.zin_dark_sway_line_cocanoor: Every hall of the Dark Lands is counted at Cocanoor.
text.zin_dark_sway_line_free: This hall is free of Cocanoor.
text.zin_dark_sway_line_yoked: This hall bears the Iron Yoke.
text.zin_dark.10.d: The raiding parties are back at Cocanoor with carts, cattle and a good deal of iron that was not theirs a month ago. The war-clans are loud and the fires are high. The Warking watches from the hall steps and says nothing, which the clans take for approval.
text.zin_dark.11.d: Riders from Cocanoor have crossed Dondor's border, burned two steadings and driven off the cattle. The Brutes of the hill farms ask what Notbuton means to do about it.
text.zin_dark.12.d: Black-iron riders have crossed our border at night and left a burned barn and a message that was not written down. The elders ask how long a hold can pretend it was not meant.
text.zin_dark.13.d: Galleys with black sails came out of the morning haze, burned the harbour and were gone before the beacons could be lit. The harbour master counts what is left of his quays.
text.zin_dark.15.d: The orcs of Cocanoor have tested the forts on Dondor's border again. It is not war. Traders on the southern road have started to take other roads, and nobody in a hall near the Dark Lands has slept easily since.
text.zin_dark.15.a: The orcs test the line again.
text.zin_dark.16.d_gol: The host has taken the forts on the march and held them. The clans bring back plunder, the Warking's name is shouted in the camps, and Dondor's riders are seen far down the road.
text.zin_dark.16.d_other: The forts on the march have fallen to Cocanoor's host. It was not a war, the heralds say, and the border has moved a day's ride south in every mind that matters.
text.zin_dark.17.d_gol: The host broke on the forts and came home without its plunder. The clans mutter, the War-Clans most of all, and the Accord is delighted.
text.zin_dark.17.d_other: The forts on the march held. Cocanoor's host went back across the border carrying its dead, and the beacons burned all night for the living.
text.zin_dark.18.d: The fighting on the march ended with nothing decided. Both sides claim they let the other go, and both sides are certain they did.
text.zin_dark.20.d: Riders from Notbuton bring an offer: a seat in the Dark Sea Accord, with its beacons, its blood-prices and its human friends across the straits. Cocanoor's fires have been seen from our wall. Whether we are safer with Dondor or with ourselves is what the elders are shouting about.
text.zin_dark.21.d_joined: The hold has taken its seat in the Accord. The Brutes find it strange to stand with orcs, and the orcs find it strange to stand with Brutes, and the beacons are lit all the same.
text.zin_dark.21.d_declined: The hold has thanked Notbuton, sent a gift of smoked fish and declined. It will watch the Accord from outside, as it watches everything.
text.zin_dark.22.d: The danger seems far, the beacons cost money, and the Accord's allies are tiring of Dondor's speeches. The elders of our hall ask whether the Accord still deserves them.
text.zin_dark.30.d: An envoy of Dondor stands in the Golden Court. The orcs of Cocanoor, he says, have started to count their neighbours' cattle. King Dunmar asks nothing of Parim but to be remembered as a friend, and Parim may decide what that is worth.
text.zin_dark.30.a: The Golden King sends his blessing.
text.zin_dark.30.c: Invite Dondor into the Lost Cause.
text.zin_dark.31.d: Dondor's envoys have crossed the dark water to Sonargur with a request for ships. They remind the Leren court of the old Grand Alliance, in which parts of the Dark Lands stood against Volgan, and they remind it that an orc kingdom on the strait is no friend to the North either.
text.zin_dark.40.d: The chiefs of the four blocs sit round the fire at Cocanoor. Sungor of the Volcano Clans wants rites, Ulgra of the Iron Clans wants forges and tithes, Britag of the War-Clans wants war, and Snikkit Many-Knives wants a seat. The Warking can hear one of them clearly.
text.zin_dark.42.d: The war-clans stand in the hall in their mail, and nobody has asked them to. They do not shout. That is worse. A king who keeps an army by its fires is a king who knows exactly how long fires last.
text.zin_dark.43.d: The war-clans have been sharpening things in the evenings, and a thoughtful orc will tell you that this is a sound of its own. The Warking has seen it before, and knows what comes after the sharpening.
text.zin_dark.44.d: The chief of an unheeded bloc has risen in the moot and named the Warking's right to rule. An orc crown is held by the arm that holds it, and the chief has brought his own arm to show. The hall waits.
text.zin_dark.45.d: The old Warking lies in the pit and the hall shouts a new name. The chief has the black iron crown and half the clans, and the half that did not choose him are weighing what it costs to be wrong.
text.zin_dark.45.a: Long may the new one last.
text.zin_dark.46.d: The challenger lies in the pit and the Warking stands over him, breathing hard. The hall is quiet for a moment, then loud. The bloc he beat will hold its peace, for now.
text.zin_dark.50.d: Riders from Cocanoor stand in our hall with a Warking's offer: the Iron Yoke. We would pay, we would host, and Goldoroth would defend us against all comers, the Warking's own host included. The elders look at one another. Black iron has been very generous to us.
text.zin_dark.50.b: Our hall answers to no one.
text.zin_dark.51.d_bowed: The hold has bent the knee. Its chief has laid his axe on the steps of Cocanoor and received it back. It is Goldoroth's now, and Goldoroth is a little larger.
text.zin_dark.51.d_refused: The hold has refused. The chief threw the Warking's gift into the yard, and the Warking's riders were sent away with their horses and their dignity. Cocanoor will remember it.
text.zin_dark.52.d: A hold that was Goldoroth's tributary has put out its hearth fire and taken a brand from the Fire-Mountain. Its hall is Cocanoor's now, whole.
text.zin_dark.60.d: A third of the Dark Lands fly Goldoroth's banner, or pay its tribute. The halls of the south look north, and the halls of the north look south. Lerendor and Parim have started to ask what lies behind Cocanoor's hall steps.
text.zin_dark.61.d: The Warking has taken the title of Great Goldoroth. The whole of the Dark Lands, from the straits to the Sea of Darkness, answers to one hall. The orcs say it has not happened before, and the old ones say it has.
text.zin_dark.62.d: Goldoroth has bent the knee to Nafeher. The Warking's black iron crown was laid on a southern step, and the host that rode out of Cocanoor will not ride out of it for anyone else. The Dark Lands wait to see what the orcs will make of having a master.
text.zin_dark.62.a: The orcs have found a master.
text.zin_dark.70.d: A hold has called the free holds to the moot stone, to agree that an attack on one will be answered by all. It is an oath between neighbours, not a crown, and it can be left as easily as it is sworn.
text.zin_dark.71.d: A hold of the Moot has been attacked, and the stone calls its sisters. The riders are at the gate. They do not demand anything. They only stand there, as men stand who know what is owed.
text.zin_dark.72.d: The moot stone stands alone. Too few halls are left to keep an oath that needed many, and the last of them has gone home to bar its gates.
text.zin_dark.75.d: A caravan of iron and honest dealing has come to the edge of the Forest Nobody Enters. Troy the Old counts it twice and sends his troll-kin south for the season. Trolls fight for pay, and are surprisingly punctual about it.
text.zin_dark.85.d: Riders from Nafeher have been found by wardens of Cocanoor in a hold's hall and sent away on foot. Goldoroth's Warking has made it known that his halls do not entertain strangers' masters. The south has taken note.
